content:
maria: Heads-up — mkdocs->docusaurus migration left a weird anchor quirk on the runtime-config page. Trailing spaces in headings are preserved in the generated id, so older deep-links 404. Example: '# Reconfigure runtime ' turned into id 'reconfigure-runtime- ' and linkcheck fails.

devon: Reproduced locally. CI linkcheck spikes on that page with 8 errors. I opened a small PR (4332) that trims heading text, but it broke one fenced code block that contains an HTML comment so the slugify step mis-parsed it.

docbot: linkcheck: docs/runtime-config.md — 8 broken links (stage). Details: https://ci.redwood-inference.local/builds/7821

developer-note: quick repro: run `python -m mkdocs build` then `grep -n "href=\"# site | sed -n '1,50p'` to see produced fragment ids.

alex: I can take the follow-up. Plan: (1) normalize heading slugs by trimming/condensing whitespace, (2) make slugify deterministic for inline code spans, (3) add a unit test for the edge-case. Will open PR 4333.

sara: For redirect/back-compat: can we add a small redirect map for the handful of old anchors? Might be faster for current customers.

patrick: I'd prefer fixing slug generation in the build pipeline rather than mass redirects. Redirects pile up and are hard to audit. If we add a plugin step that normalizes both old and new forms we can emit canonical ids and optionally generate redirects only for the handful we detect in history.

maria: Agreed with patrick. alex — can you add a toggle so we can roll the normalization plugin behind a flag? We'll enable it on staging, run linkcheck, then enable on prod.

alex: Yep. Drafting PR now. Will include benchmarks — normalization adds ~12ms to the slugify step per page in my local sampling.

devon: FYI the original PR 4332 had a commit that accidentally changed frontmatter parsing for title -> slug. That produced duplicate slugs on pages with explicit 'title:' and an H1. I'm adding a test case to ensure frontmatter doesn't override H1-derived anchors unless explicit 'slug:' is present.

maria: Good catch. Can we also add a tiny script to scan git history for common old anchor forms so we can auto-generate redirect entries if we find many occurrences?

alex: I'll add `scripts/collect_anchors.py` to PR 4333 and a flag `--emit-redirects` that writes a redirects.json snippet.

sara: Quick note for QA: when testing on staging, inspect both docusaurus and mkdocs builds — the migration still leaves some pages on mkdocs-generated artifacts in the cache. Clearing the build cache helped me reproduce the dead links consistently.

docbot: build: staging/docs — linkcheck passed on branch/pr/4333 with normalization enabled. 0 broken links.

maria: Awesome. Once PR 4333 is green and devex thumbs it I'll merge. Tagging @devex for UX check on any rendered title noise. :eyes:

devon: I'll queue the serial PR merge so it doesn't cause CI contention. Merging order: 4332 -> 4333 -> small redirect emit (if needed). Expect ~20m of staging linkcheck between merges.

patrick: If we still see edge cases, add a heuristics exception for trailing punctuation inside code spans — we saw a few anchors like 'cleanup()' becoming 'cleanup-' because of punctuation stripping logic.

maria: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a short migration note in the release changelog and ping support to watch for any customer reports.

sara: quick followup — PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4333 (draft). Please add review comments inline.

alex: Thx — will update today. :shipit:
